text.p: Digitial Equipment Corp, which reported lower earnings and revenues for its fiscal second quarter, needs to "energize and motivate" its sales force, said the publisher of a newsletter that follows the Maynard, Mass.-based computer giant.
"I think the decline in revenues is still a reflection of the Maynard musical chairs, the reorganization of Digital's sales force last summer," said Terry Shannon, publisher of "Shannon Knows DEC."
"What is good is that they managed to eek out a profit on declining revenues. What is bad is that the revenues are declining," Shannon said.
He noted that the company, in its earnings report released Thursday, made no mention of the growth rate of its AlphaServer product line.
Digital executives have touted Alpha's 64-bit system, which the company says can support all the memory ever needed for even the most complex database.
"What (Chairman Robert) Palmer needs to do is jump-start his sales force. Alpha is a good product and they clearly have price points now," Shannon said.
Digital has cut prices on its Alpha product, and earlier this month it introduced new workstations at prices that were lower than expected.
